beats.narration: BLIP-2 freezes a pretrained image encoder and an eleven-billion-parameter language model, and trains only a small bridge between them. So how much can you freeze?
beats.narration_text: BLIP-2 keeps its image encoder and its language model frozen: (1) show me what the Q-Former actually trains, (2) show me the zero-shot result against Flamingo, and (3) tell me what freezing costs.

props.command: BLIP-2 keeps its image encoder and its language model frozen: (1) show me what the Q-Former actually trains, (2) show me the zero-shot result against Flamingo, and (3) tell me what freezing costs.

beats.narration: BLIP-2 keeps both big models frozen and trains one small piece: a querying transformer that learns what to pull from an image first. The bridge, the receipt, then the bill.

props.title: BLIP-2, How Much Can You Freeze?
thesis: Freeze a pretrained image encoder and a pretrained LLM. Train only a small
querying transformer between them — and teach it what to look for first.

roadmap.label: The bridge
roadmap.body: 32 learned queries squeeze the image for the LLM.

roadmap.label: The bill
roadmap.body: What you freeze, you inherit — knowledge, limits, risks.

props.source: Li, Li, Savarese & Hoi — BLIP-2, arXiv:2301.12597 (ICML 2023)

beats.narration: Here's the audit for any frozen-backbone model. What's frozen. What actually trains. What the frozen model gets to see. And where freezing loses.
beats.narration_text: Here's the audit for any frozen-backbone model. What's frozen. What actually trains. What the frozen model gets to see. And where freezing loses.

props.heading: The freeze audit

moves.label: FROZEN
moves.detail: Which parts never update, and how big are they?

moves.label: TRAINED
moves.detail: What actually learns — and how many parameters?

moves.label: BOTTLENECK
moves.detail: How much of the image reaches the frozen LLM?

moves.label: COST
moves.detail: Where does it lose, and does the win need one LLM?

props.keepNote: Axis 3 is the rubric. A frozen LLM only knows the image through what the bridge passes on.
props.source: Receipts are BLIP-2’s own tables and sections — arXiv:2301.12597

beats.narration: The bridge is the Q-Former: a hundred and eighty-eight million parameters and thirty-two learned queries. They read the frozen image features and come out as thirty-two vectors, against the encoder's two hundred fifty-seven.
beats.narration_text: The bridge is the Q-Former: a hundred and eighty-eight million parameters and thirty-two learned queries. They read the frozen image features and come out as thirty-two vectors, against the encoder's two hundred fifty-seven.

props.heading: The Q-Former: 32 queries, one bottleneck

moves.label: Q-FORMER
moves.detail: 188M parameters: BERT-base weights plus new cross-attention.

moves.label: QUERIES
moves.detail: 32 learned queries × 768 read the image by cross-attention.

moves.label: OUTPUT
moves.detail: 32 × 768 out, against 257 × 1024 from a frozen ViT-L/14.

props.keepNote: The bottleneck: those 32 vectors are all the frozen LLM ever sees of the image.

beats.narration: Training runs in two stages. First, with only the image encoder attached, the queries learn three jobs: contrast, match, and caption. Then a linear layer turns their outputs into soft prompts for the frozen language model, which reads them like words.
beats.narration_text: Training runs in two stages. First, with only the image encoder attached, the queries learn three jobs: contrast, match, and caption. Then a linear layer turns their outputs into soft prompts for the frozen language model, which reads them like words.

props.heading: Two-stage pre-training

moves.label: STAGE 1
moves.detail: Frozen image encoder; the queries learn three losses.

moves.label: LOSSES
moves.detail: ITC contrastive · ITM matching · ITG image-grounded generation.

moves.label: STAGE 2
moves.detail: Frozen LLM; one linear layer projects the 32 outputs.

moves.label: PROMPT
moves.detail: Prepended as soft visual prompts — the LLM never updates.

props.keepNote: Stage 1 teaches the queries what to look for before any LLM is attached.

beats.narration: The receipt. Zero-shot on VQA v2, BLIP-2 with FlanT5 XXL scores sixty-five, against Flamingo eighty B's fifty-six point three, with fifty-four times fewer trainable parameters. Swap in an OPT model, and the same bridge lands near fifty-two.
beats.narration_text: The receipt. Zero-shot on VQA v2, BLIP-2 with FlanT5 XXL scores sixty-five, against Flamingo eighty B's fifty-six point three, with fifty-four times fewer trainable parameters. Swap in an OPT model, and the same bridge lands near fifty-two.

props.heading: Zero-shot VQAv2 — which LLM is frozen?
props.exception: Same bridge, OPT language models: 52.3 and 52.6 — below Flamingo80B’s 56.3.
props.source: BLIP-2 Table 2; “54x fewer trainable parameters”, abstract — arXiv:2301.12597

beats.narration: Now the bill. On OK-VQA, which needs outside knowledge, Flamingo still wins: fifty point six to forty-five point nine. The paper's explanation: the knowledge lives in the language model, and theirs is smaller.
beats.narration_text: Now the bill. On OK-VQA, which needs outside knowledge, Flamingo still wins: fifty point six to forty-five point nine. The paper's explanation: the knowledge lives in the language model, and theirs is smaller.

props.heading: OK-VQA — knowledge lives in the LLM
props.exception: The paper’s hypothesis: OK-VQA rewards world knowledge, and a 70B LLM holds more than an 11B one.

beats.narration: Two more costs. Skip the first stage and zero-shot performance drops sharply; with OPT it gets worse the longer it trains. Examples in the prompt don't help. And the frozen model's risks come along.
beats.narration_text: Two more costs. Skip the first stage and zero-shot performance drops sharply; with OPT it gets worse the longer it trains. Examples in the prompt don't help. And the frozen model's risks come along.

props.heading: What freezing costs

moves.label: NO STAGE 1
moves.detail: Zero-shot VQA drops sharply; OPT forgets as it trains.

moves.label: IN-CONTEXT
moves.detail: Few-shot examples in the prompt bring no VQA gain.

moves.label: KNOWLEDGE
moves.detail: The ceiling is the frozen LLM’s — OK-VQA showed it.

moves.label: RISKS
moves.detail: Offensive output, social bias, leaked private data.

props.keepNote: What you freeze, you inherit — its limits and its risks.

beats.narration: So freezing works, when a small bridge is taught what to look for first, and when the frozen language model already knows enough. The headline needs the right LLM. What you freeze, you inherit.
beats.narration_text: So freezing works, when a small bridge is taught what to look for first, and when the frozen language model already knows enough. The headline needs the right LLM. What you freeze, you inherit.

artifactLines: The bridge is small and real: a 188M Q-Former and 32 queries between two models it never updates.
The headline is real but conditional: 65.0 against 56.3 needs FlanT5-XXL; with OPT it lands near 52.
Stage 1 is load-bearing: without it the queries never learn what to look for.
What you freeze, you inherit: the LLM’s knowledge ceiling, no in-context gain, its risks.
props.sourceNote: Li, Li, Savarese & Hoi — BLIP-2, ICML 2023. Tables 1–2, Fig. 5, §3, §5.
